title: Write a Number in Base Seven
statement: You get an integer num. Return its base-7 representation as a string, using digits 0 to 6. Negative numbers start with a - sign followed by the base-7 digits of the absolute value. There are no leading zeros, except that zero itself is "0".

examples.why: A digit loop that runs while num > 0 never runs for 0, so 0 needs its own case.

hints: In base 10, n % 10 is the last digit and Math.floor(n / 10) drops it. What are the base-7 versions?
Repeated n % 7 gives the digits from last to first. Collect them and reverse.
Handle the sign once at the start by working with the absolute value, and handle 0 separately.

explain.intuition:
Any base works the same way as base 10. The last digit of n in base 7 is n % 7, and ⌊n / 7⌋ is the number with that digit removed. Repeat until nothing is left, and you get the digits from least to most significant; reverse them at the end.

Two edge cases sit outside the loop. Negative numbers: in JavaScript -15 % 7 is -1, and in Python it is 6, so neither gives the digit you want. Work with the absolute value and put the sign back at the end. Zero: the loop body never runs, so return "0" directly.
steps: Remember whether num is negative and set n = |num|.
While n > 0: push n % 7 as a digit and set n = ⌊n / 7⌋.
Reverse the digits, join them, and prefix - if the input was negative.
pitfalls: Taking % of a negative number directly. The result is negative in JavaScript and wraps around in Python.
Forgetting to reverse: the loop produces the lowest digit first.

solutions.title: Repeated division by 7
solutions.idea: Peel off the last base-7 digit with % 7 and drop it with integer division, then reverse.

solutions.title: Recursion
solutions.idea: The base-7 form of n is the base-7 form of ⌊n / 7⌋ followed by the digit n % 7.

followups: Convert a base-7 string back to an integer.
Support any base from 2 to 36, using letters for digits above 9.
